[Fix 2026-10-25: Gaeta is now drawn with Capua in the 1038-1039 keyframes, so this loss takes it from a state that held it; the Duchy of Gaeta page says 'In 1038, the conqueror, Pandulf of Capua, was deposed and replaced by Guaimar IV of Salerno', which the dated Guaimar IV page (June 1040) overrides; the Guaimar page's regnal table gives 'Duke of Gaeta 1040-1041'.]

1058: the siege ends with Richard as prince. 'Richard and Jordan took the princely title in 1058'; Landulf VIII 'is recorded as prince until 12 May 1062'. Mirror of norman-italy's contest_end.

1058: the Drengot counts of Aversa become the princes. 'he immediately besieged Capua and took the princely title (1058) from Pandulf's brother, Landulf VIII', who 'left the keys to the city in Lombard hands for at least four years more, until 12 May 1062'. A new house, same state: the Capua page's infobox lists the rulers from Atenulf I (887-910) to Robert II (1127-1156) under one principality.

ledger.note: 1058: the county of Aversa joins the principality. Richard I page: 'Norman count of Aversa (1049-1078)' and 'prince of Capua (1058-1078, as Richard I)'; Capua page infobox '1058: Richard of Aversa conquers Capua'. Mirror of norman-italy ledger 6 (Aversa and Capua leave that state in 1058). The county's land is Cliopatria's 120 km2 Norman Italy shape of 1034; the rest of the Caserta block is the extent reading explained in keyframe principality-of-capua_1058.

1064: Gaeta passes to the Drengot princes. 'In 1062, Richard sent his son Jordan to take Gaeta from Atenulf II'; 'Atenulf was allowed to continue personal rule until 1064', when 'Richard and Jordan appropriated the ducal and consular titles of the Gaetan rulers' (infobox 'duke of Gaeta (1064-1078)'). The Norman conquest page: Gaeta 'fully incorporated into the Drengot principality' in 1064; the Gaeta page: 'In 1064, the Lombard ruler was expelled and a Norman, William of Montreuil, took his place'.

1091: bridging year. No page dates a loss of Gaeta: it has the Norman Ridello family ruling 'from 1067 or 1068 to 1091' and, from 1103, a run of conquerors, with nothing on Capuan overlordship; Richard I's ducal title ended with his death in 1078 (infobox 'duke of Gaeta (1064-1078)'), and Jordan I died in November 1090 or 1091 (Jordan I page). 1091 closes both.

By July 1134: Roger II drives Robert II out of Capua. 'By July 1134' Roger's troops had forced the rebels to submit; Robert was expelled from Capua and Roger installed Alfonso as Prince of Capua (his entry: 'from 1135'). The Robert II page: Robert rebelled in 1132 (Roger defeated at Nocera on 24 July; the Roger page says 25 July) and was given an ultimatum by 1134. Roger had been crowned king in December 1130, hence kingdom-of-sicily; its own dossier starts the contest only in spring 1138.

July 1139: the war ends at Galluccio and Mignano. Innocent II was captured at Galluccio on 22 July 1139 and, days later, the Treaty of Mignano had the pope proclaim Roger II 'rex Siciliae ducatus Apuliae et principatus Capuae'. Between 1134 and 1139 the fighting included a Pisan fleet bringing Robert to Naples (1135), the emperor Lothair's reinstatement of Robert in Capua in spring 1137, Roger's second sack of Capua and the royal army's invasion in spring 1138 (Robert II and Roger II pages).

July 1139: the principality ends in Roger II's titles. The Capua page's body ends it at the Treaty of Mignano (1139); its infobox dates 'Roger II becomes king, duke, and prince' to 1156 and lists Robert II (1127-1156) as the last prince, and the Robert II page has Robert retake Capua in 1155 and be captured in spring 1156. Alfonso (from 1135 to his death in 1144) and then William held the title for Roger; 1139 is the body's end and the year kingdom-of-sicily dates its gain.

wars.name: Atenulf's conquest of Benevento
wars.outcome: Atenulf I defeated Radelchis II and conquered Benevento in 899; the two principalities were united under one house and declared indivisible (900 on the Pandulf Ironhead page).
wars.note: A personal union: Cliopatria keeps separate Benevento shapes and Capua keeps its own cell, so no zone is drawn. The Pandulf Ironhead page dates the 'indivisibility of the united Capua-Benevento' to 900.

wars.name: Henry II's capture of Pandulf IV
wars.outcome: 'In 1022 the prince was taken and a new prince, Pandulf, count of Teano, installed'; Pandulf IV was sent in chains to Henry II and returned only in 1026 after an 18-month siege.

wars.name: Pandulf IV's war with Naples
wars.outcome: Pandulf deposed Sergius IV of Naples in 1027; Sergius was reinstalled in 1029 by Rainulf's Normans, who received Aversa.
wars.note: The Norman-conquest page gives Sergius the grant of Aversa to Rainulf in early 1030.

wars.name: Conrad II's expedition to Capua
wars.outcome: Conrad II besieged and took Capua and gave it to Guaimar IV in May 1038; Pandulf IV fled to Constantinople; Henry III reversed it in 1047.
wars.note: The Capua page does not date the expedition.

wars.name: Norman conquest of Capua
wars.outcome: Richard of Aversa besieged Capua when its prince died in 1057 and took the princely title in 1058; Landulf VIII is recorded as prince until 12 May 1062; Aquino was seized in 1058 and Gaeta incorporated in 1064.
wars.note: The page gives the 1057 siege in one sentence. From 1058 Richard is the principality's prince, so the contest ends there although the keys of the city stayed with Landulf VIII until 12 May 1062 (Richard I page).

wars.name: Roger II's conquest of Capua
wars.outcome: Robert II was expelled by July 1134 and Roger's son Alfonso installed; Robert returned with a Pisan fleet in 1135 and with the emperor in spring 1137; Roger sacked Capua again, invaded in spring 1138 and after Galluccio (22 July 1139) was proclaimed prince of Capua at the Treaty of Mignano.
wars.note: Roger claimed the overlordship of Capua in 1127 (Capua page infobox; Roger II page, after William II of Apulia died in July 1127); Honorius II invested Robert in 1128, Robert surrendered the suzerainty to the duke of Apulia in 1129 and rebelled in 1132 (Robert II page). The vassal tint of 1129-1132 belongs on the suzerain's dossier (norman-italy or kingdom-of-sicily). The Roger II page dates Alfonso's principality 'from 1135', the sentence on the expulsion 'by July 1134'.

certainty.note: A small principality in the Campanian plain whose frontier with Naples, Benevento and Salerno is nowhere defined on the pages opened; the Norman extent (the Caserta block) is a reading.

sources.note: Capua 1058: Richard and Jordan took the princely title, Landulf VIII prince until 12 May 1062, Aquino 1058, Gaeta incorporated 1064; Aversa 1030. Re-read for the fix: 1057 siege, 1058 title, Landulf VIII until 12 May 1062, Gaeta fully incorporated in 1064, Lando forced out in 1098.

sources.title: Guaimar IV of Salerno
sources.note: Prince of Capua 1038-1047, Capua given by Conrad II in May 1038, returned to Pandulf 1047, Gaeta June 1040. Re-read for the fix: Gaeta June 1040, Sorrento July 1039 (conquered by Pandulf in 1034), Duke of Amalfi 1039-1052.

sources.title: Pandulf Ironhead
sources.note: Prince of Benevento and Capua from 943, Salerno 977/978, Spoleto 967-981, partition after March 981, indivisibility 900. Re-read for the fix: Capua and Benevento are 'two principalities under one prince' (Capua not absorbed).

sources.title: Richard I of Capua
sources.note: Count of Aversa 1049-1078, prince of Capua 1058-1078; 1058 siege and title, Landulf VIII until 12 May 1062; Gaeta 1062/1064 (duke of Gaeta 1064-1078).

sources.title: Jordan I of Capua
sources.note: Prince of Capua 1078-1091; died November 1090 or 1091 at Piperno; no extent given.

sources.title: Robert II of Capua
sources.note: Prince 1127-1156; 1128 investiture, 1129 submission, 1132 rebellion and Nocera, expelled by 1134, Pisan fleet 1135, 1137 reinstatement, 1139 Galluccio, exile, 1155-1156.

sources.title: Duchy of Gaeta
sources.note: 1032 Pandulf IV, 1038 (Pandulf replaced by Guaimar IV), 1058/1062/1064 Richard I and Jordan, Ridello family 1067/68-1091, 1135 submission to Roger, 1140 end.

sources.title: Roger II of Sicily
sources.note: 1127 claim to Capua, 1128-1130, 1132 Nocera, by July 1134 Robert expelled and Alfonso installed, 1135, 1137 sack, spring 1138 invasion, 1139 Galluccio and Mignano.

sources.title: Duchy of Sorrento
sources.note: Independent from 1027, annexed by Guaimar IV by 1040; silent on Pandulf IV 1034.

sources.title: Duchy of Amalfi
sources.note: Amalfi under Capua from 1034 and Salerno in 1039; Guiscard 1073.

notes: Page budget: 5 pages in the first pass; the 2026-10-25 repair opened seven more (Richard I, Jordan I and Robert II of Capua, Duchy of Gaeta, Roger II of Sicily, Duchy of Sorrento, Duchy of Amalfi) and re-read the Capua, Norman-conquest, Guaimar IV and Pandulf Ironhead pages. No page gives an infobox area, so the area comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's shape is one 253-432 km2 cell for most years, two to three cells in 1028-1039. Life span: the dossier now runs 861 to July 1139 (Treaty of Mignano), through the Norman princes (Drengot: Richard I 1058, Jordan I 1078, Richard II 1090/91, Jordan II to 1127, Robert II 1127-1156) as a rename in 1058; the Capua page's body ends at 1139 and its infobox at 1156 (Robert II retook Capua in 1155 and was captured in spring 1156; Alfonso 1135-1144 and William held the title for Roger meanwhile), and the kingdom-of-sicily dossier dates its gain 1139. Extent: Cliopatria's Capua shapes are a single city cell that lies about 8 km west of the city itself; every keyframe now adds a 12 km circle round Capua. For 1058-1139 no page gives the extent; the Caserta province (plus Aversa's cell) is used because norman-italy removes it from Cliopatria's Norman Italy shape from 1085 and kingdom-of-sicily draws it as the Principality's in 1138-1139; if the orchestrator prefers the documented cells only (Capua, Aversa, Gaeta 1064-1090) the keyframes principality-of-capua_1058, _1064 and _1091 shrink to them. Cliopatria gaps filled with new keyframes: 866-874, 900-989, 1010-1014, 1029-1033, 1038 and 1039 (Gaeta and Sorrento), 1047-1055, 1058-1063, 1064-1090, 1091-1139; 1040-1046 has no shape (Guaimar IV of Salerno held the principality; the Salerno dossier carries it). The Cliopatria 1028 shape keeps the Naples cells to 1033 although Naples was restored in 1029. Personal unions: Capua and Benevento under Atenulf I (899/900), Pandulf Ironhead (943-981) and Landulf VII (1000-1007) were 'two principalities under one prince' (Pandulf Ironhead page), not one absorbed in the other, so Capua keeps its own keyframes 900-989 and 1010-1014; the duchy-of-benevento dossier, whose Cliopatria shapes of those years contain the Capua cell and which records 'gains' of Capua in 899 and 1010, double-draws them (orchestrator decision). Not drawn: Lando's hold of the city of Capua 1090-1098 (no rebel dossier); the 1129-1132 vassalage of Robert II to the duke of Apulia (the suzerain's dossier carries vassal events); Aquino (seized 1058). Counterparts without dossiers: 'Duchy of Gaeta' (1032, 1040, 1064, 1091 events), 'Duchy of Sorrento' (1034 gain). Gazetteer lacks Gaeta, Sorrento and Aversa as places. Rulers omitted: no page gives a dated list. The 849 (decree) and 851 (Divisio) dates are both on the Capua page; the Salerno page gives 851 only.
